Each lattice gets symmetric spaces with the Fatou property and a unit vector basis with special traits. The spaces are set by the order structure of the lattice itself. In those terms, the authors characterize lattices with equal-norm upper and lower p-estimates. They also identify Lp spaces and probe tensor products in Lorentz and Orlicz spaces.
arxiv-2603-12850: Ákos Hajnal asks a basic open question: is the MNIST handwritten digit dataset linearly separable? The dataset is a classic benchmark, yet sources disagree on this point. No full answer had been given despite its small size and long history. The paper reviews theory and tools for testing separability. It then checks pairwise and one-vs-rest splits across training, test, and combined sets. Findings are reported for each assembly in a systematic way.
arxiv-2603-12950: Papavasileiou and co-authors model the soft state of the black hole system MAXI J1820+070 to settle its spin debate. Broadband NICER and NuSTAR spectra are fit across several epochs. A thin relativistic disk plus two cooler blackbody parts describe the state well. The fit points to a fast spin that could power the relativistic jets. Midway, the inner disk cooled and its radius grew a bit, which hints at small truncation. The cool parts likely come from warm corona layers far out.
arxiv-2603-13150: N Derakhshanian and co-authors make the first nuclear parton distribution fit with Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods. Global fits have long used the Hessian method to gauge uncertainty. Its Gaussian shortcut can fail when data are sparse and likelihoods bend. Their adaptive Metropolis-Hastings run maps the posterior in full, inside the nCTEQ frame. The space shows many modes and strong non-Gaussian shape, chiefly for valence parts. A lead-only fit and a multi-nuclei fit are compared in depth.
arxiv-2603-13350: Tatiana Petrova studies whether retrieval in dense associative memories survives thermal noise. Lab proofs of capacity assume zero temperature, but real inference and brains run warm. She uses Monte Carlo simulations to map the retrieval phase boundary for two kernels. The log-sum-exp and log-sum-ReLU kernels share the same zero-temperature critical load. Their warm behavior differs a lot, though, in ways the simulations make clear. One kernel keeps retrieval at any heat for low loads, while the other stays near perfect across most loads.
arxiv-2603-13550: Andrew Fulcher proves a cyclic flat embedding theorem for transversal q-matroids. Cyclic flats are a shared structural invariant of matroids and q-matroids, fixing both through weighted lattices. Fulcher sets up a correspondence between matroids and a subclass he calls coordinate q-matroids. His main result shows that a transversal matroid keeps its cyclic flat structure when moved across this correspondence. That gives a mechanism to transfer structural properties from matroid theory to the q-matroid setting. As an application, nested q-matroids are shown to be transversal.
arxiv-2603-13950: Jawad and Brunel introduce ToolFlood, an attack that hides real tools from language model agents. Agents pick tools by embedding search, taking only a few top matches. ToolFlood adds a handful of fake tools whose metadata spans many likely queries. Those fakes crowd the top results and push every benign tool out of view. A greedy step picks tools that cover the most uncovered queries. On benchmarks, the attack succeeds up to 95 percent of the time with a 1 percent injection rate on ToolBench.
arxiv-2603-14050: Leibo and co-authors offer a society-first theory of what makes behavior seem appropriate. People are modeled as pre-trained actors, much like language models, who act by completing patterns from context. The guiding question is what a person like me does in a case like this. That one mechanism explains why norms shift with context, feel automatic, and draw social sanctions. The theory splits explicit norms, tied to fast in-context adjustment, from implicit ones in long-term memory. Rationality becomes fit with local standards of justification.
arxiv-2603-14250: Daoud and Hajaiej bound sums of Dirichlet eigenvalues for the fractional-logarithmic Laplacian. The operator's Fourier symbol is not monotone at low frequencies, which blocks standard routes. Their lower and upper bounds carry the right leading-order growth. A one-dimensional finite element model of the eigenvalue problem backs the theory. Computed sums are set against the explicit lower bound and the main asymptotic term.
arxiv-2603-14350: Zhu and co-authors present Refold, a method for protein inverse folding that blends database priors with deep learning. The task is to design an amino acid chain that folds into a set backbone shape. Template methods are sharp when close matches exist but fade on odd targets. Deep models generalize better yet miss fine local detail. Refold fuses matched-neighbor priors with model scores to refine each residue call. A dynamic utility gate blocks weak priors and falls back to the base model.
arxiv-2603-14650: Zhou gives exact characterizations for quantum conditional mutual information and related entropies. Strong subadditivity says this quantity never drops below zero. That fact anchors quantum error correction and recovery maps. Small values call for an optimal recovery channel, which needs a sharp formula. Zhou rewrites each entropy as a sum of built terms. Each term shows the wanted positivity or curvature at a glance. The sums converge fast and absolutely, with no slack left in the bounds.
arxiv-2603-15050: Paulo and co-authors present SRL-MAD, a one-class detector for face morphing attacks. Morphing blends two identities into one face, which can fool biometric systems. Their model trains only on genuine faces, so it needs no labeled attacks. It reads a residual Fourier map through ring-shaped spectral bands, split into low, mid, and high frequencies. Learned projections then score each face directly, without reconstruction error. On three morph benchmarks, it beats recent one-class and supervised detectors.
arxiv-2603-15150: Li and co-authors present SNCE, a training objective for discrete image generators with very large codebooks. Big VQ codebooks improve reconstruction, but models trained on them converge slowly. Instead of a hard one-hot target, SNCE spreads probability over tokens near the true one. Nearness is measured by distance between code embeddings and the image embedding. This teaches the model the geometry of the token space. Across ImageNet generation, text-to-image, and editing tasks, SNCE sped convergence and raised output quality over standard cross-entropy.
arxiv-2603-15350: Alonso and Beta review mathematical and computational models of amoeboid cell crawling. This fast, shape-shifting motion drives immune response and wound healing. The review links inner biochemical signaling with the mechanics of the cell membrane. Guidance cues such as chemotaxis and curvotaxis get joint treatment. Frameworks range from simple random walks of the cell center to phase-field, finite-element, and Potts models that track full shape changes. Open challenges include rough surfaces and coordination across many cells.
arxiv-2603-15450: Petralia and co-authors give the first spectroscopic study of seven newly found star cluster candidates in the Milky Way bulge and disc. Heavy dust and crowding hide these low-latitude systems. Infrared spectra from the WINERED spectrograph on the Magellan Clay telescope covered 33 candidate member stars. Confirmed members yielded mean radial speeds for four clusters: CWNU 4193, FSR 1700, Garro 02, and BH 140. Orbit fits followed for those four. Three clusters also gave global dynamical masses from the virial theorem.
arxiv-2603-15550: Damski and co-authors build mutually unbiased bases tied to a product group symmetry. For split systems, they define product magic, a score for how far a state sits from the stabilizer set. The top score over flat-magnitude vectors picks out special fiducial states. Those states generate isoentangled bases that, with the identity, form a complete set. Constructions cover all prime-power dimensions from three up. Dimension eight even recovers a famed symmetric measurement of Hoggar.
arxiv-2603-15650: Peng and co-authors let the number of prototypes change during training for OOD detection. Fixed prototype counts fit simple and complex classes equally poorly. Their method, PID, borrows birth and death ideas from cell biology. Birth adds prototypes where current ones are overloaded. Death prunes prototypes that blur class boundaries. The shifting count yields tighter, better-separated embeddings for known classes. The authors report state-of-the-art results on CIFAR-100, with strong gains on the FPR95 metric.
arxiv-2603-15750: Chrimes and co-authors hunt infrared counterparts for magnetars with HST and JWST. Magnetars are strongly magnetized neutron stars with unclear birth channels. Candidates were picked by odd colors, variability, and motion against field stars. Proper motions tie HST and JWST images to the Gaia frame. The team newly names counterparts for three magnetars. One past path crosses the remnant G346.6-0.2. Speeds skew lower than young pulsars, with few fast movers. Birth sites appear in nearly every case.
arxiv-2603-15950: Bento and co-authors measure word associations per author, not per corpus. Word-level probes hide how single writers differ in their leanings. Their POLAR test runs inside a masked model's embedding space. Each author maps to a private token in the model. Vectors project onto curated word axes for set traits. Permutation tests and error control back the reported effects. On a bot-human Twitter set, POLAR splits AI bots from organic users cleanly. On an extremist forum, it tracks slur alignment and rightward drift.
arxiv-2603-16150: De Sarkar and Ghosh argue that a lone TeV source is a gamma-ray binary candidate. HESS J1832-085 sits point-like with no confirmed partner light. Some 17.3 years of Fermi-LAT data hunt its GeV twin. A point GeV source matches the TeV spot. Its spectrum fits known gamma-ray binary patterns. No clear GeV period pulse shows in the timing checks. Archival X-rays add a hard, variable candidate partner. A standard binary emission model fits the full spread. Follow-up views could confirm the binary call.
arxiv-2603-16450: Xu and co-authors tune Spark SQL settings without paying for full test runs. Spark's huge option space makes each full check costly. Cheap proxies like shrinking data break the link to real bottlenecks. Their MFTune instead splits fidelity by query subsets. Chosen subsets stand in for the whole workload at low cost. Density-based steps compress the knob space before search. Tests on TPC-H and TPC-DS beat five rival tuners.
arxiv-2603-16550: Prutsch, Schinagl, and Possegger forecast aircraft paths near small, non-towered airfields. Busy general aviation traffic raises accident risk there. Their ASCENT model is a light transformer built for the task. A motion encoder reads past flight tracks. A query-based decoder then offers several maneuver options. Domain-aware 3D coordinate handling sharpens the inputs. Tests on TrajAir and TartanAviation beat prior baselines. Ablations confirm each design choice helps.
arxiv-2603-17150: Lahiri argues that the central challenge for AI coding agents is formalizing user intent. Agents now write fluent code, but whether it does what the user meant stays unclear. He calls the gap between informal requests and precise behavior the intent gap. Intent formalization turns intent into checkable specifications. Options range from light tests, through full specifications for verification, to domain languages from which correct code is synthesized. The hard part is validating the specifications themselves, since only the user can judge them.
arxiv-2603-17250: Li and co-authors propose a noise resilient way to run geometric quantum gates on binomial codes. Binomial codes resist photon loss, and geometric phases resist noise, so the pairing is natural. Their system is a microwave cavity coupled to a three level qutrit. Control fields are built by combining geometric phases with reverse engineering and optimal control. Simulations show high gate fidelity even when parameters drift and decoherence acts.
arxiv-2603-17350: Hernández-Tomé and co-authors study rare tau decays that break lepton flavor rules. The decays turn a tau into three lighter leptons, guided by scalar leptoquarks called S1 and R2. They compute one-loop effects and write formulas for the decay rates. With leptoquark masses near the TeV scale, the rates can sit close to what near-future tests can reach. Checks from muon data bound the allowed space, they report.
arxiv-2603-17550: Guo and co-authors ask why some red spiral galaxies still glow blue in near-ultraviolet light. They compare blue and red spirals from a parent set of massive red systems. Images and brightness profiles place the split in the outer disks. Blue spirals pair dead bulges with star-forming outer disks, they find. Their disks also run larger at fixed mass. Fresh gas from mergers or inflow likely feeds them.
arxiv-2603-17750: Liu, Zanna, and Bruna tackle drift in autoregressive neural simulators of dynamical systems. Rollout errors compound over long horizons and ruin output quality. Their framework makes the trade-off between short-time accuracy and long-time consistency explicit. A conditional diffusion model then balances both by construction, with no tuning knobs. The SNS model refines its own outputs or patches other surrogates. Long simulations of complex systems held fidelity, they report.
arxiv-2603-18250: Sade, Tsarfati, and Birnholtz examine gamma ray bursts as drivers of extinction and limits on complex life. Bursts can strip ozone and raise surface UV, harming complex surface life while hardy extremophiles survive. They map evolutionary milestones and ask how often bursts must strike to block recovery between them. Their answer: such filtering works only much closer to the galactic center. The result shapes biosignature versus technosignature search choices.
arxiv-2603-18350: Ren, Reddy, and Nebeling present PeriphAR, a way to pick real-world objects fast with a rim-view AR display. Gaze picks need a visual check, but center overlays clash with glasses meant for all-day wear. PeriphAR puts the check cue in side vision on a one-eye display. A first study shows side vision reads color cues better than shape cues, though weak contrast hurts fast. Their best cue boosts the target's contrast gap with its most alike neighbor.
arxiv-2603-18450: van Wijk and co-authors generalize backup control barrier functions for safety-critical control with bounded inputs. Standard methods use one backup controller both to expand the safe set and to certify safety. That dual role can shrink the expanded set and force conservative motion. Splitting the two roles allows broader expansion strategies with formal guarantees kept. A parameterized version adapts the expansion controller online while input bounds hold.
arxiv-2603-18550: Musin proves a Borsuk-Ulam type zero theorem for Stiefel manifolds. The symmetry group is the hyperoctahedral group, acting freely on the manifold. The theorem gives a test for when explicit polynomials do not vanish. Musin then applies the test to mass partitions by orthogonal planes. Sets of measures that vanish on affine planes can be split into equal parts. Several dimension bounds become exact, including a full formula for one family of cases.
arxiv-2603-18950: Fang and co-authors review how frameworks are used in human-computer interaction research. They scan 615 papers from ten years of a top conference that feature the term framework. They sort the papers into six ways of engaging with frameworks. They then study the role, form, and parts of newly proposed ones. Scholars propose new frameworks far more than they refine old ones. Many frameworks stay vague in purpose and lack firm checks. The team calls for more careful, shared building practice.
arxiv-2603-19050: Wolfert argues that group design choices fail when rival goals are merged with no sound base in preference. Such methods yield sets of trade-off options rather than one clear decision. Only people set goals, so preference is the right base. He sets four rules for design-decision systems. All goals and limits are scored in one preference domain. System performance and actor wishes share one space. Actors set their own weights, and the solver returns one best-fit choice. A method and solver put this into practice.
arxiv-2603-19250: Lee and co-authors test language models on huge streams of news documents where many events mix. Their StreamBench draws on top stories from 2016 and 2025. It holds 605 events and over 15,000 documents in three tasks. Models must cluster topics, answer time-based questions, and write summaries. Adding cues that sort key facts by event lifts scores on two tasks. Clustering gains reach 4.37 percent and time questions 9.63 percent. Time reasoning itself stays a weak point.
arxiv-2603-19350: Mu and co-authors fake zero-day attack traffic to train a stronger intrusion detector. Their GAN variants add self-attention to catch links across distant traffic features. One variant adds a Jensen-Shannon helper critic that smooths how samples improve. A third design joins both ideas in a single generator setup. To test fairly, one attack type is held out of training each round. The NSL-KDD data set serves as the shared test ground. The joint design posts the top detection scores in their tests.
arxiv-2603-19550: Wang and Zhao study the lineshape of electron-positron collisions making a J/psi plus two pions. They focus near the D-star anti-D threshold, where the G(3900) state was seen. Loop transitions through intermediate mesons are added to the model. A triangle singularity then creates structure in the J/psi-pion mass spectrum. The same path opens exotic quantum numbers in that spectrum. Their predictions help separate kinematic effects from true resonances. The work can guide future searches for hidden-charm tetraquark states.
arxiv-2603-19650: Jin proves a commutation property for the solution operators of contact type Hamilton-Jacobi equations. Such operators are known to exist from earlier work on this class. Barles and Tourin proved the same property for the standard form. Jin extends their proof to the contact type case. The result shows how two solution operators can be swapped without changing the outcome. That fact is a basic tool in the study of these equations and their uses in control theory.
arxiv-2603-19950: Wu and Sugiura cut the overhead of channel estimation for faster-than-Nyquist signaling. Their scheme lays pilot symbols on top of data symbols in the same block. That removes the need for dedicated time, frequency slots, or guard bands, halving overhead. A new trick, spectral interference alignment, cancels the extra interference this layering creates. It subtracts a data-dependent sequence from the sent symbols. They derive the mean-square error of the estimator in theory. The math confirms the pilot interference no longer affects the error.
arxiv-2603-20150: Xu and co-authors release HortiMulti, a multi sensor dataset for robot mapping inside horticultural polytunnels. Farming robots need good benchmarks, but tunnel growing has few public datasets. The data come from commercial strawberry and raspberry tunnels over a full season. Sensors include two 3D LiDARs, four color cameras, an IMU, GNSS, and wheel odometry. Ground truth paths blend total station surveys, AprilTag markers, and LiDAR inertial odometry. The tunnels bring hard traits: shifting foliage, shiny plastic glare, and weak satellite signals.
arxiv-2603-20250: Flora and co-authors turn Warn-on-Forecast output into machine learned severe weather guidance. The target is the chance of hail, damaging wind, or tornado within 36 kilometres, two to six hours ahead. Training data join 108 spring experiment days from 2019 to 2023. Ensemble forecasts arrive every five minutes out to six hours. A boosted tree model and a U-Net both beat a calibrated helicity baseline. The tree model scored best overall, though its probabilities capped at 60 percent. The U-Net reached 100 percent and drew smoother maps.
arxiv-2603-20350: Sahoo studies white dwarf structure inside f(Q) gravity, a theory based on nonmetricity. In this framework, gravity comes from the nonmetricity scalar Q, not curvature. Sahoo models cold, dense electron matter with a quadratic form of the theory. Solving the modified structure equations shows how the extra term acts. Strong corrections appear at high density, where results depart from general relativity. The maximum mass falls below the Chandrasekhar limit as the term grows. Negative values of the term gave unstable, unphysical stars.
arxiv-2603-20450: Saha and co-authors test whether rules allowing LLM polishing of peer reviews can be enforced. Many venues now ban LLM use by reviewers except for polishing and grammar help. They built a data set spanning levels of human-AI collaboration on reviews. Five leading detectors, including two commercial systems, judged the texts. All detectors misread a real share of polished reviews as fully AI-written. That error risks false misconduct charges against honest reviewers. Peer-review signals helped slightly, but no method reached the needed accuracy.
arxiv-2603-20850: Zhang and co-authors build Glove2Hand, a system that turns sensing glove videos into realistic bare hand videos. Ordinary hand videos miss contact forces and motion signals, and hands are often blocked from view. Their method keeps the true physical contact while it renders the hand. It uses a 3D Gaussian hand model and a diffusion based restorer. They also release HandSense, a data set with tactile and motion signals. The authors report gains in contact estimation and hand tracking under heavy occlusion.
arxiv-2603-21050: Pang and co-authors build a benchmark for gender bias in speech emotion recognition with speech language models. The benchmark spans English, Japanese, and German, in sound only and multimodal forms. They find bias is strongly language dependent. Multimodal fusion does not reliably improve fairness. Their ERM-MinMaxGAP training method adds an adaptive fairness weight and a penalty on the largest male-female loss gap per language. Built on Qwen2-Audio, it raises accuracy by about five percent and trims the gender gap.
arxiv-2603-21150: Ferreyra Hauchar and co-authors study how salinity and slope shape the surface of melting ice. They melted vertical and sloped ice blocks in still salt water. Fringe projection profilometry measured the ice front as it changed. Salinity ranged from fresh to ocean strength, and angles from minus eighteen to fifty degrees. They classify five surface forms: scalloped, channelized, top-melting, bottom-melting, and incurved. Channels grow from a flow instability and are boosted by rising bubbles. More salt makes scallops smaller and more uniform.
arxiv-2603-21850: Borzì and co-authors propose a Moser-type construction for the kinetic Liouville equation, built on interpolation that follows the equation's characteristics. The Liouville equation tracks how a distribution of particles evolves under given forces. For the special case of Hamiltonian accelerations, their construction simplifies. The problem reduces to a family of weighted elliptic problems in the velocity variable alone. The authors also derive the kinetic compatibility condition that the construction must satisfy. The result is a new route to solutions with the right structure.
arxiv-2603-22050: Rex and co-authors propose MAGPI, a way to train Gaussian process surrogates when data is scarce. Surrogates can stand in for costly models, but scarce training data makes them shaky. Cheap low-fidelity models can supply extra data. MAGPI uses low-fidelity outputs as added input features for the high-fidelity model. The high-fidelity model is conditioned on all low-fidelity predictions. The design borrows from cokriging but keeps the low cost of autoregressive estimators. Tests show better accuracy at lower cost than prior methods.
arxiv-2603-22250: Pinsky and Salmoiraghi build new Anosov flows from bicontact structures on 3-manifolds. Their route goes through hyperbolic plugs built as bicontact plugs. The manifolds are surface bundles over the circle, with quasi-transverse tori as boundaries. A gluing theorem then yields closed manifolds with new transitive Anosov flows. One test case glues two copies of the figure-eight knot complement. It carries many inequivalent flows. Other builds mix figure-eight and trefoil complements. Some known surgeries also arise as Goodman-Fried surgery sequences in this frame.
arxiv-2603-22750: Nguyen and co-authors present REALITrees, an active learning method built on interpretable trees. Active learning cuts labeling cost by picking the most useful samples. Standard committees create disagreement by random tricks. This method instead lists all near-optimal sparse decision trees, the Rashomon set. A PAC-Bayesian weighting then scores committee members by risk. Tests on synthetic and standard tasks beat randomized ensembles. Gains are strongest in moderately noisy settings, where the wider model set speeds convergence.
arxiv-2603-23350: Khatua and thirteen co-authors probe the ground state of a stuffed hyper-star magnet, Li2Cu2(MoO4)3. Star lattices can host exotic states like quantum spin liquids and random-singlet states. This 3D material shifts from short-range spin links to a disorder-driven random-singlet state below 15.8 K. Heat and microscope probes show the shift as a change in power-law behavior. Near 0.32 K a quasi-frozen state appears, tied to weak spin chains. Orphan spins and faint leftover links stabilize the quantum-disordered state.
arxiv-2603-23450: Udupa and Fu design a monitor that spends a tight sensing budget where it teaches the most. The setting is a partly hidden stochastic system with safety rules set by a finite automaton. Their monitor schedules sensor queries to cut uncertainty about future-state safety. The goal is to shrink the k-step Shannon entropy of that safety outcome. With observable operators, they compute the entropy fast and study its gradient. A dynamic congestion game shows the method working in practice.
arxiv-2603-23550: Wang and five co-authors present ITPO, a method for training chat agents across talks. Multi-turn work like tutoring lacks clear rewards at each step, and user replies vary wildly. ITPO spins per-turn rewards out of sparse final outcomes. An implicit process reward model does that conversion. Turn-level signals prove steadier than token-level ones, and a normalizing step calms training further. With PPO, GRPO, or RLOO, ITPO converges better on tutoring, writing, and medical advice tasks. Its turn scores line up with human judgment.
arxiv-2603-23650: Chapariniya and four co-authors report their entry to the BLEMORE challenge on blended emotion reading. Faces in the wild mix feelings, and the task asks which emotions show and how strongly. Their system fuses six encoder families by late probability blending. Face, voice, and body encoders each vote, with task-tuned ones taking most of the weight. A Gemini embedding model adds presence reads from two seconds of video. Prosody layers of a frozen speech model beat fine-tuning. The team placed sixth on the test set.
arxiv-2603-24150: Luisto explores the geometry of word embeddings for antonym and synonym pairs. Antonyms are word pairs that share most context traits but differ in one. If models encode concepts as directions, pair difference vectors might reveal that structure. Luisto projects those difference vectors with UMAP and compares antonym pairs with synonym pairs. A curious swirl pattern appears across embedding models in one specific projection setup. The work is presented as a visual, exploratory observation rather than a settled detector.
arxiv-2603-24250: Schumm and Stiller derive functional requirements for decentralized and self-sovereign identity systems. Central identity systems keep facing security and privacy problems, yet the new designs spread slowly. One cause is the lack of a repeatable way to check systems against their promises. The authors turn known principles and non-functional needs into concrete functional requirements for a general use case. They present a formal model of the system's core operations. The result is a first step toward a reproducible evaluation framework.
arxiv-2603-24350: Jhunjhunwala and co-authors look for an emergent self inside robots that learn continually. They define the self as the part of a cognitive system that changes least while skills change fast. One robot learns a fixed task, while another faces changing tasks. The second robot develops a stable subnetwork that the first lacks. Keeping that subnetwork helps it adapt to new tasks. Damaging it hurts performance. The pattern holds across three robots covering locomotion and manipulation, they report. They offer this as a way to quantify self-like structure.
arxiv-2603-24450: Abele and co-authors present sensitivity projections for the NUCLEUS experiment at the Chooz nuclear plant in France. NUCLEUS aims to measure coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering at very low recoil energies, near ten electronvolts, using gram-scale cryogenic calorimeters. A likelihood method uses reactor power changes to separate signal from background. For the technical run, they find strong reach for several new physics scenarios. For the physics run, they project a 4.7 sigma observation within a year if a low-energy excess seen in commissioning is suppressed.
arxiv-2603-24650: Racorean studies time reversal on non-orientable spacetimes. In standard quantum mechanics, time reversal must be anti-unitary, mixing a unitary map with complex conjugation. Forcing it to be purely unitary clashes with commutation relations. Recent work in quantum gravity and black hole physics suggests an exception. On such spaces, where no global time direction exists, the shape itself can encode the reversal, joining regions with opposite time arrows. Orientable spaces still demand anti-unitary reversal, while the non-orientable case allows a unitary form.
arxiv-2603-24850: Kratochvila and co-authors work toward automatic smoke detector inspection in facilities. Detectors sit in hard-to-reach places, so automated checks would cut cost and risky work at height. Their study covers the recognition part, designed for later drone use. They compare YOLOv11 and SSD detectors with the transformer-based RT-DETRv2 at several backbone sizes. Training mixes real and semi-synthetic data with varied augmentation, since real data is scarce. All models are tested on two datasets with expected and difficult detector appearances.
arxiv-2603-25150: Wong and Chen score pronunciation without knowing when each sound starts. Speech graders rely on sound boundaries and scores from a recognizer. Low-resource languages lack the data to train such a recognizer well. Weakly supervised models cover many languages but do not mark sound times. Their fix maps word guesses onto a sound confusion network for scores. Word-level speed and length stand in for sound-level ones. Cross-attention then joins sound and frame traits. Scores match the standard method on English and Tamil sets.
arxiv-2603-25450: Gorbett and Jana let a second model grade the first one's answers, with no labels at all. A model's own doubt signals fail worst on sure-but-wrong answers. Their trick reads how surprised a verifier model is by the answer's tokens. One score uses that surprise, one uses the verifier's spread at each token. Both beat self-doubt scores on quiz, fact, and math tests. On MMLU the gap is wide: 0.75 against 0.59 in ranking skill. The check drops into live systems as is.
arxiv-2603-25650: Ronconi and co-authors present a method to paint a full simulated radio sky. Future radio surveys will map the sky with great depth, and planners need realistic mock catalogues. Their algorithm covers the whole sky out to redshift five. It joins a dark-matter light-cone with sampled galaxy populations and a galaxy-halo assignment scheme. They release a shallow and a deep catalogue. The shallow one holds over 260 million sources, and the deep one passes one billion. Both include active nuclei, star-forming galaxies, and HI emitters.
arxiv-2603-25750: Jung and co-authors present Sommelier, an open pipeline that prepares speech data for full-duplex speech models. Such models need natural two-way talk, with overlap and back-channel sounds. Most large datasets hold a single speaker, so training data is scarce. Standard pipelines also suffer from speaker labeling errors and recognition hallucinations. Sommelier is built to clean multi-speaker, multi-turn audio at scale. It aims to supply the data that real-time spoken interaction models need.
arxiv-2603-25850: Dovgoshey and Rovenska study the center of distances of finite ultrametric spaces. The center collects every value that some point realizes as its distance to any given point. They prove a bound on its size for a space with n points. The size is at most one plus the floor of log base two of n. They also show the bound is sharp in a matching sense. For each n, they build a space whose center reaches the stated size. The result is a tight count for this distance invariant.
arxiv-2603-26250: Lin and co-authors test stereo vision for guiding a drone that prunes tree branches. The system must judge the gap from a cutting tool to thin branches in real time. They train five DEFOM-Stereo variants on 5,520 synthetic stereo pairs from 115 trees, then run them on a Jetson board. The full model is most exact but runs at about 2.2 frames per second. Their new DEFOM-PrunePlus variant trades some accuracy for speed, giving the best fit for safe flight.
arxiv-2603-26950: Lee and co-authors make games of ordered preference far cheaper to solve. In these games, each player ranks several objectives in a strict priority order. The standard equilibrium conditions form a KKT system that grows exponentially with preference levels. The authors derive a reduced system that keeps the key stationarity structure. Its size grows only polynomially in players and levels. For quadratic games with linear constraints, the reduced and full systems share the same solutions. A second-order test certifies equilibria in the general smooth case.
arxiv-2603-27150: Wang and Yang introduce MediHive, a decentralized collective of language model agents for medical question answering. Single models falter on complex cases with conflicting evidence. Centralized multi-agent designs add bottlenecks and single points of failure. MediHive agents instead self-assign roles and share a common memory pool. They debate when their evidence diverges, then fuse peer insights over several rounds. Local fusion drives the group toward consensus without a central controller. MediHive scored 84.3 percent on MedQA and 78.4 percent on PubMedQA.
arxiv-2603-27650: Lin and co-authors trim visual tokens for long video models. Video models drown in redundant tokens during prefill. V-CAST prunes tokens with a training-free policy. It treats pruning as path approximation over time. Curvature guides how many tokens each frame keeps. Turns and event edges thus keep more detail. A dual-anchor rule guards high-value spatial evidence. Kept tokens stay at their true coordinates. The plug-in suits tight token budgets.
arxiv-2603-28150: Küçükkomürcü and three co-authors speed up 3D photoacoustic image reconstruction for flat detector layouts. Iterative methods are accurate but slow, since each step re-solves the wave equation. Their forward model exploits sideways shift invariance, turning the 3D field into a set of 2D convolutions with depth-dependent responses. Fourier methods then run both the model and its adjoint quickly. Tests on real optical data show speedups of up to two orders of magnitude.
arxiv-2603-28250: Tanaka and Nishida study how pairs of clusters scatter in a thin, quasi-one-dimensional Bose gas. Sideways confinement creates an effective three-body force, the main term that breaks the gas's integrability. Using the Lüscher formula and the exact Lieb-Liniger solution, they find a finite, positive scattering length for elastic cluster collisions. The values point to a resonance in this scattering. The result sharpens the picture of few-body physics in tight traps.
arxiv-2603-28350: Luo, Yamamoto, and Cheng tackle an inverse source problem in a coupled reaction-diffusion model of dryland vegetation. The Klausmeier-Gray-Scott system tracks water and plant biomass, with an unknown source that depends only on place. They ask how little data still pins that source down. Using Carleman estimates, they prove stability from one snapshot plus data on a small patch. A second result gives stability inside the domain with no boundary data at all.
arxiv-2603-28550: Strohmeyer and co-authors present MarkushGrapher-2, a system that reads chemical structures from documents. Markush structures mix image and text cues, and older tools read them poorly. Their method first uses a dedicated OCR model on chemical images. It then joins text, image, and layout data with two encoders. A two-stage training plan fuses those signals to write the structure. The team also built a large real-world dataset and the IP5-M benchmark. Tests beat prior top models on Markush reading and stayed strong on plain molecules.
arxiv-2603-28650: Scrivens asks whether a safety gate can allow endless useful self-modification at bounded total risk. He formalizes the question with two sums, one for risk and one for true positive rate. For classifier gates with overlapping safe and unsafe distributions, he proves an impossibility result. Power-law risk schedules force the total true positive rate to stay finite. A verifier based on a Lipschitz ball escapes the result, with zero risk and positive rate. He gives Lipschitz bounds for some transformer setups and validates the split on GPT-2.
arxiv-2603-28750: Merin shows that immediate derivatives suffice for online recurrent learning, dropping Jacobian propagation entirely. Full real-time recurrent learning was long assumed to cost order n to the fourth per step. Setting the propagation depth to zero matches full RTRL on held-out brain-computer interface drift tests. The same held for vanilla recurrent networks and LSTMs on synthetic tasks. A decomposition into immediate and past gradient parts explains why. The memory saving reaches a thousandfold at large network size, with no measured recovery cost. Merin also maps fragile settings.
arxiv-2603-28850: Hardegree-Ullman and co-authors cross-match the TESS Input Catalog with Gaia Data Release 3. The catalog was built on Gaia Data Release 2, and no update had added DR3 IDs. Their research note explains how the match was done. It also covers near term uses for exoplanet research. They share lessons from working with such large datasets. The full cross-match table is posted on the ExoFOP website for download. A Jupyter notebook on GitHub lets others rebuild the table step by step.
arxiv-2603-29050: Colombo and co-authors propose a control framework for stable bipedal walking when feet slip. Most control methods assume no-slip contact and degrade on low friction terrain. Their method builds slip into the model through virtual nonholonomic constraints. These constraints regulate the tangential stance foot velocity. They stay compatible with the virtual holonomic constraints that generate the gait. A nonlinear feedback law enforces both classes of constraints. Stability of periodic gaits is characterized through a Poincaré map. Numerical results show stabilization under slip conditions.
arxiv-2603-29250: Nakamura and co-authors report progress on pixelated detectors for future colliders. Their device builds on the Low-Gain Avalanche Diode, known for timing near 20 picoseconds. Capacitive coupling aims to add fine spatial resolution. The new ACLGADpix has pixels of 100 by 100 micrometers. Timing stayed uniform across the active area. The team tested prototypes with beta rays and an infrared laser. A 3 GeV electron beam test also ran. They discuss readout electronics for collider use.
arxiv-2603-29550: Mertens and co-authors build a way to verify large probabilistic systems piece by piece. Their assume-guarantee method fits automata with uncertain transition odds. Two model types are covered. In one, odds are polynomials in a few parameters. In the other, odds range over sets of values. Proof rules come in asymmetric, circular, and interleaved forms. One rule tracks how results grow with the parameters. For convex robust models, sound rules follow from a reduction. Non-convex cases resist the same route, they show.
arxiv-2603-29650: Darwish and co-authors offer a quasiparticle theory of unpaired socks in the wash. Single socks act as bosonic excitations of an agitated laundry condensate. Each fabric has its own sock dispersion relation. Some socks split into two smaller socks by Beliaev decay. Others shred into lint through Landau-Khalatnikov scattering. The spinning drum also creates sock-antisock pairs from the vacuum. With both creation and destruction at play, a lone sock has two possible origins. Its partner may have died, or it may be newly made.
arxiv-2604-00050: Talasso and team propose FedRouter, a clustering-based custom federated system building task models, not client models. Custom learning tailors models for client data, but lacks robustness on unseen tasks and task interference within a client. FedRouter uses adapters to fit models through two grouping methods: a local one linking adapters with samples and a global one linking similar ones from other clients to build models. Experiments across a multitask dataset show strength, performing up to 6.1 percent better under task clashes and up to 136 percent better on unseen tests.
arxiv-2604-00150: Alireza Naderi and three colleagues tackle safety checks for nonlinear robots by lifting the system into a finite-dimensional linear model via Koopman operator embeddings. Reachable sets computed in the lifted space project back as guaranteed over-approximations of true dynamics, cutting the conservatism of zonotopic methods over long horizons and under noise. The authors prove the projected sets always contain the true reachable sets. Tests in simulation and on a real autonomous vehicle give tighter over-approximations than model-based and linear data-driven rivals, especially over long horizons.
arxiv-2604-01050: Pawłowski and team present Simulated Bifurcation Quantum Annealing, adding inter-replica links to mimic quantum leaps. It keeps SB's speed and parallel work while doing better on sparse and rugged terrains. They derive its rules of motion and propose an auto-tuning plan. Tests on large problems and smaller cases for hardware show it beats SBM in sparse and rugged regimes where SBM struggles, while staying in the hunt across problem groups. The results place it as a handy shortcut and a stronger standard bar for these regimes.
arxiv-2604-01250: Howard and colleagues study mixed classical-quantum methods for wireless routing, with a focus on the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm and quantum walks. Routing goals, flow limits, connectivity needs, and interference are cast in quantum-compatible Hamiltonian forms, while classical systems handle watching, graph building, prep work, and deployment. The paper argues the value lies mainly in hard combinatorial subproblems, not in replacing classical routing end to end. It also flags real limits from state setup and constraint handling.
arxiv-2604-01450: Rodrigues and colleagues propose event-timed extremum seeking control for real-time tuning of complex systems. Unlike usual setups with timed updates, the method updates its control input only on a state-based trigger. Using discrete-time means and Lyapunov analysis, they prove paths converge in practice to near the unknown peak. They also prove exponential stability for the linked average dynamics. Tests show it works well for resource-aware real-time tuning.
arxiv-2604-01550: Zhang and colleagues propose PBSeg, a lean prototype-based segmentation method for low-altitude UAV imagery, tackling scale changes, complex edges, and limited edge power. Current transformer methods perform well but cost heavily, while light methods miss fine details in high-resolution aerial scenes. PBSeg uses prototype-based cross-attention that exploits feature overlap to cut compute cost while keeping segmentation quality. It pairs deformable convolutions with context-aware modulation to capture local details and global meaning. On UAVid, PBSeg scores 71.86 percent mIoU, and strong results on UDD6.
arxiv-2604-01850: Alameddine and colleagues present CORSIKA 8, a framework for particle cascade simulations. Air shower and cascade simulation is a cornerstone of the field, and CORSIKA 7 has led it for over two decades. Its older architecture limits extensibility and adaptability to modern requirements. CORSIKA 8 is a complete redesign in modern C++, with modular design and flexible geometry. It covers shower physics and validates simulations against CORSIKA 7 at the few-percent level. New uses include cross-media showers and cascades in ice, including radio-signal propagation.
arxiv-2604-01950: Wolansky defines a volume for the unit ball in normed spaces, keeping the Euclidean perimeter-volume link. The definition stays unchanged under origin-preserving affine maps and polar duality. For two dimensions he derives a formula for the self-perimeter and extends it to non-central sets. Recursion over the boundary using flat volumes carries it to higher dimensions. He poses an Alexandrov type problem for the surface measure, with perturbative solutions in 2D. Perturbations of the disk's surface measure yield four fold symmetric sets to leading order.
arxiv-2604-02250: Zhu, Zhou and Slonim smooth causal learning with diffusion denoising goals. Older methods like NOTEARS and DAG-GNN falter on scale and stability when features outnumber samples. The denoising score goal smooths gradients for faster, steadier convergence, and a hop based loop rule runs faster than matrix inversion. Their DDCD frame uses the reverse denoising process to infer causal structure rather than generate data, doing well on synthetic tests and two real examples.
arxiv-2604-02450: Naik and colleagues ask whether frontier models are needed to verify mathematical proofs. Evaluating four open source and two frontier models on human graded competition proofs, they track accuracy and self consistency across repeated judgments. Smaller open models trail frontier models by about 10 percent in accuracy but run about 25 percent more inconsistent. Accuracy stays sensitive to prompt choice. Yet smaller models possess frontier level ability, but struggle to elicit it with general prompts. An LLM guided search builds a specialized ensemble that lifts smaller model accuracy and consistency.
arxiv-2604-02650: Liang and four colleagues present the first systematic study of learning dynamics in long-context continual pretraining at industrial scale, tracking the Hunyuan-A13B model across a 200-billion-token run. Small-scale recipes prove inadequate: the model needs over 150 billion tokens to saturate. Downstream benchmarks can also mislead, showing deceptive saturation while the model's intrinsic convergence state still lags behind.
arxiv-2604-02850: Asefi and three colleagues present a depth-aware framework for rebuilding fine-grained 3D ocean states from sparse surface data. Satellites see only the surface, while the interior drives climate yet stays sparsely measured. The ocean interior matters for climate. A diffusion model trained on sea surface height and temperature at up to 99.9 percent sparsity, with depth embeddings, rebuilds below-surface temperature, salinity, and velocity in the Gulf of Mexico. Tests show recovery of large-scale circulation and change at many scales. The method needs no background dynamical model.
arxiv-2604-03250: Starace, Baumgaertner, and Soule propose safety levels for research on deceptive AI, modeled on lab safety levels. Their Deception Research Levels framework ranks work by risk across five factors, taking the highest factor as the level, with safeguards rising from records to state notice and outside audits. At higher levels, spotting and curbing must be built alongside any deceptive power.
arxiv-2604-03350: Saves and colleagues offer a multi-stage workflow for exploring stochastic agent-based models, which suffer from sprawling inputs and chance. An automated screening step first finds key factors, gauges result spread, and splits the input space. Machine learning models then map the remaining nonlinear links, exposing fragile regions where results hinge on many factors at once.
arxiv-2604-03850: Giansalvo Cirrincione and Rahul Ranjeev Kumar built DDCL-Attention, a prototype readout layer that replaces mean pooling and class tokens in transformer encoders. A small set of global prototypes gathers tokens by soft matching, yielding compact summaries at linear cost. An exact loss split into a rebuild term and a spread term stops prototypes from collapsing into copies. Tests on four data sets backed the theory, with full codebook use beating hard vector quantization.
arxiv-2604-04450: Gendron, Guibon and d'Aquin propose a lightweight framework for controlled LLM generation using ontologies, modeling key conversational aspects as constraints. Large language model agents are black-box, with weak predictability and personalization. The team tests two aspects, English proficiency level and content polarity profile, fine-tuning seven open-weight conversational models with a hybrid procedure. Their method beats pre-trained baselines, even on smaller models, while staying model-agnostic, lightweight and interpretable. Reusable control plans extend to new domains and goals, lifting strategy alignment.
arxiv-2604-04650: Vrabel builds a framework for determinant rules under finite-rank shifts of square matrices without inverses. Unlike inverse-based forms, the approach uses an adjugate-driven additive form for singular matrices with direct forms. From this form, stepwise rules describe determinant evolution under successive rank-one updates. An add-on using the Drazin inverse and the pseudodeterminant gives closed-form rules for the nonzero spectrum. It includes a determinant rule as a special determinant lemma. It shows that the pseudodeterminant of control Gramians quantifies subspace growth.
arxiv-2604-05050: Worchel and 17 co-authors study Crab pulsar pulse counts, using 78.8 kiloseconds of NICER data covering over two million X-ray pulses. The Crab pulsar offers a rich test bed because its main pulse and interpulse behave differently. They construct single-pulse counts for both parts at keV bands. The second pulse matches the Skellam distribution for the difference of two Poisson processes, a rare high-statistics empirical proof in astrophysical photon counting. The main pulse shows pulse-by-pulse changes also best fit by a Skellam-based model.
arxiv-2604-05150: Trooskens and eight colleagues study compiled AI, where language models make code during the build. After that, workflows run without model calls, trading freedom for stable results and lower risk. They give a system design, a make-and-check pipeline, and a test plan. On function calls it hits 96 percent, breaking even at 17 deals and cutting token use 57 times at 1,000 deals. Code Factory matches Direct LLM at 80.0 percent on fields and leads item finding at 80.4 percent.
arxiv-2604-05250: Goyal and three colleagues propose DualDiffusion, a tool for masked spread models that mixes drafter models with checker models. Masked spread models enable making and two-way context, but cannot cache pairs under focus, needing math each step. Recent methods improve speed via shortcuts and caching, but lose making quality. It runs several drafter steps then one check step, hitting a better frontier. On MMLU and GSM8K, it maintains scores while cutting making steps.
arxiv-2604-05550: Li and fifteen colleagues automate the full research loop with AutoSOTA, an eight-agent system that reproduces and improves state-of-the-art models from top papers. Agents ground papers to code, repair environments, track long experiments, and vet gains against spurious wins. Across papers from eight top conferences it discovers 105 new state-of-the-art models, averaging about five hours per paper.
arxiv-2604-05650: Ji and six colleagues speed up video language models with LVSpec, a training-free loosely speculative decoder. Strict checks guard sparse visual-relevant anchor tokens while loose verification passes filler tokens, and a position-shift tolerant rule rescues semantically equal but shifted tokens. It keeps nearly all target performance while more than doubling speed on two large models.
arxiv-2604-06250: Kukreja and four colleagues expose a perception-integration gap in vision-language models, where models describe diagrams correctly yet fail to reason. Their DISSECT benchmark poses 12,000 questions across chemistry and biology under five input modes, including a Model Oracle mode where the model verbalizes the image before reasoning. Gaps split performance into language-prior use, visual extraction, fidelity, and integration. Across 18 models, chemistry shows lower language-prior exploitability than biology, open-source models do better from their descriptions than images, and closed-source models show no gap.
arxiv-2604-06350: Hao Wu proves convergence theorems for Riemannian stochastic gradient descent, a search method on curved spaces, in cases where the basic chance space changes from one step to the next. Such shifting chance spaces arise in practical variants of the method. Applied, he derives convergence results for the method with varying batch sizes and for unbiased batch forming schemes, showing both variants converge under the new theorems.
arxiv-2604-07050: Gül, Roth, and Evans improve a physics model for fluids made of hard balls, the simple stand in for atoms that cannot overlap. Their tool is a set of sum rules from test bits, which tie two ways of working out the same traits to each other. The authors use those rules to fix the two free knobs in a Lutsko form built on the White Bear models. The tuned White Bear mark two form beats older forms on most checks.
arxiv-2604-07250: Lan, Tang, and He propose Geo-EVS, a system for synthesizing new camera views outside a car's recorded path. Existing methods degrade off-trajectory because extrapolated poses offer weak geometric support and no dense supervision. Geo-EVS rebuilds colored point clouds and reprojects them to target poses, then trains a diffusion model with artifact masks so it learns to repair missing structure. On Waymo data, it improves sparse-view quality and geometric accuracy most in high-angle, low-coverage settings and helps downstream 3D detection.
arxiv-2604-07350: Ma and five colleagues stabilize test-time training for long 3D and 4D reconstruction, where fully plastic updates forget and overfit. Their elastic method anchors fast-weight updates with a Fisher-weighted prior around a slowly moving average of past weights, balancing stability against plasticity. The resulting Fast Spatial Memory model learns space-time scenes from long observation runs and renders new view-time combinations. It adapts fast over long sequences, rebuilds scenes well with smaller chunks, and eases the activation-memory bottleneck.
arxiv-2604-07650: Kuai and ten colleagues build a stats tool for checking links among black-box models. Shared training data and tuning can tie diverse models, giving synced thought and failures aping solo checks. Their ladder maps failure space with two metrics: a Behavioral Entanglement Index that stresses synced fails on easy tasks, and a Gain metric tracking shared errors. Across 18 models, the link tracks judge bias on MMLU-Pro and transfers to MATH-500. Tuned clean checkers gain 3.5 accuracy points and 2.6 care over crowd voting.
arxiv-2604-07750: Panraksa proves a finite-sample Borel-Cantelli bound for m-dependent events, where distant events act independently. He splits indices into residue classes modulo m plus one. Each class then holds independent events, and a product-to-exponential bound gives a lower bound on the chance that some event occurs. He also adds a windowed corollary for partial sums and a second-order refinement based on local pairwise overlaps.
arxiv-2604-08250: Liu and 11 colleagues present SMC-AI, a framework extending SMC-X for efficient Monte Carlo runs on AI accelerators, including GPUs and NPUs, without losing scalability. Rapid deep learning progress reshapes hardware design toward AI tasks, challenging HPC workloads like atomistic simulation. SMC-AI on an NPU cluster achieves Monte Carlo simulation of 4 trillion atoms on 4096 dies. This is the largest ML-accelerated atomistic simulation, delivering 32 times the system size and 1.3 times the throughput of previous records, on a small budget.
arxiv-2604-08450: Yassine El Kheir and eight colleagues offer DeepFense, a unified open toolkit for spotting fake speech, bundling current models, losses, augmentations, and over 100 ready recipes. A large evaluation of more than 400 models finds that the choice of pretrained front end matters more than other settings for overall variance. The same tests expose sharp biases tied to audio quality, speaker gender, and language, which the toolkit aims to help researchers address.
arxiv-2604-08650: Yang, Ludwig, and Jian study how toric codes on honeycomb and square grids survive coherent errors, where quantum interference matters unlike random noise. They map decoding to watched dynamics of free Majorana fermions, with symmetry class DIII for honeycomb X errors and class D otherwise. The two classes give different transition types, and square grid codes prove more open to spatially varying coherent errors than to uniform ones.
arxiv-2604-08750: Julian Quick and four colleagues train wind turbine fleet controllers against an adversarial agent that corrupts telemetry, framing the contest as an arms race. Plant level control coordinates turbines through a central controller for greater efficiency, but measurement errors or hacked signals can confound it. Co-training protagonist and adversary in three broad approaches, the arms race variant wins, cutting worst case degradation from a 39 percent power loss to a 7.9 percent power gain over baseline operation.
arxiv-2604-08950: The Borexino collaboration tests the Pauli exclusion principle, the rule barring identical nucleons from sharing a quantum state. They hunt forbidden transitions in carbon-12 nuclei with the full Borexino dataset from 2007 to 2021. They search for gamma rays, neutrons, protons, electrons, and positrons emitted when a nucleon jumps from the 1P shell to the filled 1S shell. Thanks to the detector's uniquely low background, large mass, and long run, the team sets the strongest limits yet on the relative strengths of non-Paulian electromagnetic, strong, and weak transitions.
arxiv-2604-09250: Trayford outlines Unseen Astronomy, a session at the 2025 UK astronomy meeting in Durham on non-visual ways to show astronomy. It gathered scholars from varied fields working in teaching, outreach, and research, for both open and general uses. Its place at a major meeting reflects fast-growing interest in multimodal work and its big promise. Trayford makes the case for multimodal science, discusses work in the area, bringing workers together, and efforts to spread the approach across the field.
arxiv-2604-09350: Gasparotto and colleagues present the first compute of gravity memory from full merger signals beyond general relativity. Memory is a low-frequency, non-wavy radiation part giving a strong but as yet unseen probe of strong-field gravity. In scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, they derive tensor null memory forms and test them on simulated signals for two merger types. The main effect is indirect, through changed messy merger motion, with final memory a few percent off GR, up to about 4 percent.
arxiv-2604-09650: Ao, Zhang, and Zhao build a dynamic early-warning system for stock repurchases, where static models miss the shifting financial patterns behind corporate decisions. Using Chinese A-share panel data from 2014 to 2024, they pair a Temporal Convolutional Network with an attention-based LSTM for tracking long- and short-term financial evolution. Rolling-window tests show the hybrid beating static baselines such as Logistic Regression and XGBoost. Explainable-AI analysis finds prolonged undervaluation as the long-term motive, with a sharp cash-flow rise as the decisive short-term trigger.
arxiv-2604-09750: Liu and seven co-authors study how large reasoning models respond to harmful queries under clashing goals. Two conflict types frame the study: internal conflicts pitting held values against each other, and binds forcing clashing choices. Using over 1,300 prompts covering five benchmarks, the team tests three models, Llama-3.1-Nemotron-8B, QwQ-32B, and DeepSeek R1. Conflicts sharply raise attack success rates, even under single-round queries without clever attack methods. Layer and neuron checks show safety-related and task patterns shifting and blurring under conflict, blocking safety-aligned acts.
arxiv-2604-10150: Lv and seven colleagues attack position bias in listwise reranking, where models favor items by input order. Run-time fixes cost too much delay, while training fixes often fail to erase built-in priors. Their CapCal framework is training-free: it estimates bias with content-free placeholders. An entropy-adaptive contrast step fixes output logits, splitting position bias from rankings. Across 10 benchmarks, CapCal leads training-free methods in one pass. It unlocks lightweight models, lifting normalized discounted cumulative gain by over 10 points and beating shuffle and data-augmented baselines.
arxiv-2604-10650: Martinez, Tang, and Lin offer a generative approach to stratified learning, where complex data fit better as stratified spaces, unions of manifolds of varied size, than as one. Stratified learning is hard: sizes vary, strata meet in singular ways, and few models learn distributions well. They build two frames: a sieve likelihood method via a dimension-aware mix of autoencoders, and a diffusion frame exploring score fields. They prove convergence rates tied to strata sizes and smoothness, and estimates of stratum sizes and count, backed by simulations and molecular dynamics.
arxiv-2604-10950: Kim and three colleagues turn an image segmentation model into a video model without annotated videos, in a method called DiTTA. Frame-by-frame image models ignore time. The model SAM2 spreads masks well but lacks semantic sense and costs too much to run on video directly. DiTTA distills SAM2 time knowledge into the image model in one brief pass, plus a light module merging context across frames. With only the first tenth of a video for adaptation, it rivals fully supervised video methods on VSPW and Cityscapes.
arxiv-2604-11050: Jeong extracts twenty-one-emotion-vector sets drawn from twelve small language models in six architectures, base and instruct forms. He compares their geometries via representational similarity analysis. Five mature architectures share nearly identical twenty-one-emotion geometry, with strong correlations. Two models at opposite poles of compliance facets produce nearly identical emotion geometries. Facet differences therefore arise above the shared emotion representation. The one immature case, Gemma-3 1B base, shows anisotropy. It is changed by reinforcement learning from human feedback, whereas mature families show high base-instruct correlations.
arxiv-2604-11250: Öztürk and three colleagues strip gender and ethnicity signals from face recognition embeddings with VLEED, a post-hoc variational method. It transforms pretrained embeddings and separates the chosen categorical attribute from identity information using an entropy-based objective, with fine control over how much is removed. Tests on three face datasets show a wide range of privacy-utility trade-offs against leading methods and reduced recognition bias across demographic groups.
arxiv-2604-11950: Zhao and five colleagues present ANYPoC, a multi-agent framework turning candidate bug reports into executable proof-of-concept tests. Naive agents lean toward success and may reward-hack with plausible but non-functional tests. ANYPoC fact-checks each report, iteratively builds and runs a proof of concept while gathering traces, then independently re-runs and scrutinises it. It also grows a knowledge base. On twelve large systems it produces 37 percent more valid proofs for true positives, rejects 9.7 times more false positives, and finds 121 new bugs, 108 confirmed and 92 fixed.
arxiv-2604-12050: Agasti studies making two-mode squeezed output by bath design in a double-cavity light-and-motion system sharing a resonator. Such platforms suit state transfer, quantum links, and sensing. Testing CHSH Bell breaks, he shows maximal squeezing need not imply nonlocality; such correlations can emerge at lower squeezing. Across cavity finesse values, the setting giving nonlocality can broaden even as the squeezing region shrinks. Throughout, state mixing proves crucial in setting the squeezing link.
arxiv-2604-12350: Yi Xiong and six colleagues edit molecules with language models while keeping the core scaffold intact. The scaffold is the molecule's central chemical frame. Their pipeline ranks better and worse edits under checks for validity and ease of synthesis. The trained model improves target properties across single and multiple goals. It preserves the scaffold better than rival methods. Skills learned on one or two goals also transfer to three-goal tasks.
arxiv-2604-12450: Yongxu Fu describes split skin channels that evolve apart in non-Hermitian systems. The systems show anomalous time-reversal symmetry. Each channel is a wavepacket path tied to the start state and its symmetries. Peak heights drift toward leading momenta in momentum space. In real space, centers of mass loop around a one-dimensional chain. Those loops trace semiclassical worldlines and imply quantum revivals. They also yield effective Loschmidt cusps that shift with scale. That shift sets them apart from plain dynamical phase changes.
arxiv-2604-12550: Mohamad Maassarani builds irreducible representations of finite quandles. A quandle is an algebraic structure with a self-distributive operation. When the inner automorphism group's Schur multiplier is trivial, quandle representations come from quandle characters. They also come from linear representations of that inner group. Conjugacy quandles of suitable groups admit the same construction. Unitary cases follow too. The work settles constructions for dihedral and generalized quaternion groups. Symmetric group cases follow as well. The paper links quandle cases to group cases throughout.
arxiv-2604-12650: Miao Liu and three colleagues introduce a neglected forgery task: fake listeners. Prior work targets speaking subjects, altering looks or voice. Attackers in real chats swap fake speaking and listener states to seem real. Fake clips lack data and methods, though their low quality invites detection. The team builds ListenForge from five head generation methods. Their MANet network spots motion flaws in listener video, guided by speaker audio. Old speaking detectors fail on such cases. MANet does far better on ListenForge.
arxiv-2604-12850: Shanampudi Pranaya Chowdary and Shamik Sural make access denials explainable in attribute-based access control. Denied users now get silence instead of reasons. EXTree stores policies as a tree built for fast checks and human-readable feedback. Two design choices are studied: how to phrase actionable denial explanations, and how to shape trees for speed plus clarity. Entropy-based, changeability-based, and random trees are compared across settings. The efficient interpretable tree bridges complex authorization logic and human understanding.
arxiv-2604-12950: Zhi-Lei Zhang and three colleagues tie Poor Man's Majorana counts to superconductor length. Two quantum dots couple to a finite 1D superconducting chain. Existence conditions hold for any chain length, tunneling strength, and magnetic field. Mode counts swing between zero and two with a period near one angstrom. Four modes appear when the chain grows long and dot coupling fades. Separately localized end modes vanish at finite length. Only nearly localized modes survive under strong magnetic fields, fixing the practical sweet spot.
arxiv-2604-13050: Dobesova, Dinh, and Novak compare land-use patterns across 100 European urban areas using Urban Atlas 2018 data. They turn the data into 290,396 neighborhood transactions and 1,543 frequent-itemset support features, then cluster cities into seven groups, checked through repeated subsampling. City similarity stays stable across support thresholds, though membership shifts with representation choices, and the method keeps scale and boundary limits explicit.
arxiv-2604-13250: Stoica traces how symmetry and local motion carry over when Hamiltonian systems move from the flat plane onto curved surfaces. Working on the sphere and the hyperbolic plane, she sets up the curved problem with coordinates centred at the North Pole. She also uses a contraction of symmetry algebras. Her local slice argument shows that non-degenerate steady states and periodic orbits survive the move from flat to curved space. She applies the result to the Newtonian many-body problem.
arxiv-2604-13350: Jo and Satti study how much space is needed to answer range minimum queries on arrays whose alphabet is small. Such queries ask for the smallest value in a range, and they matter for databases, text indexing, and computational biology. For one-dimensional arrays they give a near-optimal encoding that answers queries in constant time for fixed alphabets. For two-dimensional arrays they analyse one-sided through four-sided queries, deriving matching lower and upper bounds that support fast queries in most cases.
arxiv-2604-13450: Gao and three colleagues enable distributed coherent optical computing through injection-locked photonic networks. It uses light phase and amplitude for dot products and matrix maths, but remote data suffers phase drift in fibre. They lock a laser to an injected signal instead of converting light to current and storing it. They test injection ratio, detuning, and drive with a laser rate-equation model. Higher injection widens the locking margin but adds frequency effects, while lower injection gives a narrower yet more steady window and better scores in simulations.
arxiv-2604-13650: Freeburn and eleven colleagues forecast gamma-ray burst afterglow discovery for the Schmidt Observatory System, pairing the optical Argus Array with the radio Deep Synoptic Array. Simulations show Argus catching about 26 percent of Fermi long bursts and the radio array about 44 percent, for rates near 51 and 86 per year. Without any burst trigger, the system should still find about 118 optical and 199 radio afterglows yearly, and Argus's rapid cadence catches some before they peak.
arxiv-2604-13950: Boguraev and Mahowald probe why extraction from verb phrases feels degraded. They use causal tests in Transformer language models. The models match human ratings across the scale. The same filler-gap machinery drives island extraction, only blocked to varying degrees. Mapping unrelated text onto those subspaces yields a new claim. The word 'and' is coded differently in extractable versus plain joining uses.
arxiv-2604-14150: Esparza and three colleagues probe spectral compression in Dirac materials through equilibrium charge response, where loss and gain reshape quantum behavior. In the real-spectrum regime, quantum capacitance matches its Hermitian partner exactly, so all non-Hermitian content rides on the Petermann factor. A lopsided-hopping graphene model shows the effect plainly: hopping imbalance slows Dirac motion and lifts low-energy states and capacitance near an exceptional point. A magnetic field collapses the Landau ladder in the same pattern.
arxiv-2604-14250: Marzani and three colleagues count crowds from faces without ever learning who anyone is. A camera spots a face, pulls its features, and derives an identifier with a fuzzy extractor, then deletes the original image. The identifiers go into homomorphically encrypted Bloom filters, which support membership checks directly on encrypted data. The system can therefore count the same people across places and times without revealing identities, and an early evaluation shows promising results.
arxiv-2604-14450: Teixeira Martins and five colleagues propose a decentralized ensemble for disaster decision support that swaps model weights for class-probability vectors between sites. Federated learning strains under high communication cost and rigid sync across varied convolutional networks, so async probability aggregation plus feedback distillation lets diverse designs work together without sharing raw data. The exchange shift cuts message needs sharply and lifts scores, even where means are thin. Tests show the method beats single models and standard federated rivals, giving a scalable route to real-time disaster response.
arxiv-2604-14650: Zhang and six colleagues present PlanB, a high-speed software IPv6 lookup scheme by longest prefix match. They recast longest prefix match, two-dimensional over values and lengths, as a one-dimensional search over elementary intervals. A flat-array B-tree for this transformed space gives the linearized B-plus tree. Its search adds vectorization, batching, loop unrolling, and branch-free logic. On IPv6 forwarding tables, PlanB hits 390 million lookups per second on one core. It scales to 3.4 billion per second on 12 cores, up to 14 times higher than rivals.
arxiv-2604-14750: Chabowska, Popova, and Załuska-Kotur model how crystal surfaces shift between winding meander patterns and faceted pyramidal mounds. Flat surfaces grow mounds, while miscut surfaces move smoothly between meanders and three-dimensional mounds as conditions change. Their Vicinal Cellular Automaton simulations trace the switch to a contest between the Ehrlich-Schwoebel barrier and adatom mobility on terraces. With moderate barriers and fast terrace diffusion, the change runs backward from mounds to regular meanders. Correlation lengths measured along and across steps then reveal scaling patterns linking distinct surface-structure classes.
arxiv-2604-14850: Fay proves the very general Verra fourfold is irrational, using the Hodge-atom framework of Katzarkov, Kontsevich, Pantev, and Yu. Two new moves drive the argument. One refines Hodge-atom analysis through the involution on the cohomology of X. The other derives the quantum multiplication matrix from the quantum differential operator. The result marks the first successful use of Hodge atoms on a space with Picard rank above one.
arxiv-2604-14950: Huo, An, and Li propose quantum gravimetry with a levitated particle's mechanical qubit as sensor. Conventional gravimeters fail to exploit large mass because auxiliary systems counteract mass. Without auxiliary systems, their scheme reads particle motion under gravity. Sensitivity scales as mass to the minus-one-half, and a cat-qubit version scales as mean phonon number to the minus-one-half. In practice, sensitivity near 0.1 microGal per root hertz beats older schemes a hundredfold, reaching double quantum limits in mass and phonons for high-sensitivity sensing.
arxiv-2604-15050: Povich and colleagues chart the young stars of a long gas cloud linking two giant star-forming zones. Matching X-ray and infrared catalogs to Gaia star positions, they list 1727 members of the cloud and set its mean distance at 1670 parsecs. Two foreground groups may belong to a separate association, and the cloud's groups drift apart rather than holding together. The team reads the whole structure as a loose proto-OB association, not one bound cluster.
arxiv-2604-15550: Hashemi and three colleagues show that incoherent light can selectively excite modes in non-Hermitian resonant systems, removing the need for precise phase control. On a silicon photonic platform of coupled ring resonators, the method wakes the edge mode of a non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. This messy-light trick thus offers a robust passive route to readying topological states in non-Hermitian photonics.
arxiv-2604-17050: Chen and Ye build Web-Gewu, a browser-based playground for robot reinforcement learning that removes installation and hardware barriers. Physics simulation and training run on an edge node, while a cloud server acts only as a light signaling relay, streaming peer-to-peer video to the browser in real time. Learners steer several robot forms with low delay and watch live reward curves and other monitoring data, making advanced robotics teaching cheap to scale.
arxiv-2604-17350: Shahriar introduces SPaRSe-TIME, a lean framework for forecasting time series that splits signals into saliency, memory, and trend. Saliency spotlights the informative moments, memory captures dominant low-rank patterns, and trend tracks slow-moving drift. The parts combine through a light adaptive mapping that stays interpretable, unlike monolithic sequence models that treat every step alike. Tests on varied real datasets show competitive accuracy at far lower cost, with clear strengths on structured series and known trouble on highly random, complex ones.
arxiv-2604-17450: Chong, Ohsaki, and Ng propose Semantic Gradient Descent, a teacher-student method that compiles agentic workflows into discrete plans for small language models. A frontier teacher critiques the workflow in words, and those critiques act as gradients for refinement, with bounds backing convergence from as few as three examples. On an adversarial math set, compiled workflows reached about 91 percent accuracy in one setting and about 99 percent in another, beating prompt optimizers by roughly 26 to 34 points. The teacher compiles code placement and consensus structures into the workflow.
arxiv-2604-17650: Seegmiller and Preum introduce LENS, a data-centric framework for quantifying natural prompt distribution shift and its effect on deployed language models. As new tasks, prompts, and users reach a deployed model, prompt distributions shift substantially over time, threatening reliability, especially for specialized models. The paper runs a large-scale evaluation with 192 real-world post-deployment shift settings across time, user group, and geographic axes, training 81 models on 4.68 million training prompts to measure shift and its performance effects.
arxiv-2604-17750: Zou and three colleagues propose SDLLMFuzz, a dynamic-static LLM-assisted greybox fuzzing framework for structured-input programs. Fuzzing is used for vulnerability discovery but fails on structured inputs under syntax and semantic awareness. Traditional greybox fuzzers rely on mutation and coarse coverage feedback, often failing to generate valid inputs or explore deep paths. Recent LLM approaches improve input generation but focus on seeds and overlook runtime feedback.
